The city council voted seven to two on Wednesday to add dedicated bus lanes on three of the busiest corridors, after a public hearing that ran past midnight.

Supporters said the lanes would cut average commute times, while opponents argued that removing parking would hurt small shops along the route.

The transit agency estimated construction would cost about twelve million, most of it covered by a state grant awarded earlier this year.

Work on the first corridor is expected to start in the autumn, with the remaining two to follow over the next eighteen months.
